questions.a: Two or more substances physically combined in any ratio, each keeping its properties.

questions.q: Name two properties of a compound that mixtures lack.
questions.a: Fixed composition and properties entirely different from its elements.

questions.q: Why is air a mixture and water a compound?
questions.a: Air's gases can be separated physically and vary in ratio; water has fixed H:O ratio joined chemically.

concepts.title: Separation by Filtration, Evaporation and Decantation

questions.q: How does filtration separate a mixture?
questions.a: The filter lets the liquid pass while holding back insoluble solid particles.

questions.q: When is evaporation used for separation?
questions.a: To recover a dissolved solid from its solution, as salt from sea water.
Heavy particles settle (sedimentation) and the clear liquid above is poured off (decantation).

concepts.title: Advanced Separation: Distillation, Chromatography and More

questions.a: Separating a liquid from dissolved solids, or two liquids with different boiling points.

questions.q: What is centrifugation? Give a daily-life example.
questions.a: Spinning a mixture so heavy parts settle; washing machines spin-dry clothes and dairies separate cream.

questions.q: How is chromatography useful for inks?
questions.a: Different dyes travel different distances on paper, separating into coloured bands.
